sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: 1H 2026 consolidated revenue was US$173.0m, only 0.5% above 1H 2025, because the coal arm's lower ASP and volumes offset the waste platform's first full half [S12]. We model FY2026E at 1.5% (the run-rate, not the Q1 spike), then 6%/5%/4%/3% as the HPS-funded waste build annualises and the 46 MWp floating solar starts producing [S15, S12].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the last actual: 1H 2026 gross profit was US$28.228m on US$173.016m of revenue, a 16.3% margin, as the waste mix rose to 61% and coal cash cost fell to US$38.2/t [S12, F23, F22]. We hold 16.3% through FY2027E and fade to 16.0% long run rather than applying an unsourced margin squeeze; a 2pp uplift from further waste mix is left to the bull case, not the base [S12, S15].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The data pack's 11.4% is wrong: the LK shows selling and G&A expenses of US$71.95m against US$380.2m of segment revenue in FY2025 (18.9% of the reported US$365.9m consolidated revenue), and 1H 2026 sales and G&A were US$33.172m on US$173.016m (19.2%) [S17, S12, F96]. We hold the 1H 2026 run-rate of 19.2% rather than the previous 19.5%, which had no source [S12].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The full FY2025 D&A charge is US$74.121m (F81: fixed assets 22.205 + mine amortisation 31.317 + right-of-use 11.790 + intangibles 8.809), 20.3% of FY2025 revenue, and the engine history now carries that full charge, not the pack's 15.7 or the fixed-asset 22.2 alone [S8]. For the forecast we use the post-divestment 1H 2026 run-rate: adjusted EBITDA 25.733 plus operating loss 4.770 implies a D&A plus PLN/other add-back of 30.503 on revenue 173.016 (17.6%, F98). The 20.3% FY2025 ratio includes divested-PLTU depreciation and higher mine amortisation and is not the forward run-rate [S12].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was US$47.1m (12.9% of revenue), including mine-property additions of US$37.2m and fixed assets of US$9.8m [S8]. The 46 MWp floating-solar project is 65% complete with COD targeted for Q4 2026, so capex stays elevated: 10% in FY2026E, 9% in FY2027E and 8% long run [S12].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was US$9.1m on US$365.9m of revenue (2.5%), and the group describes disciplined working-capital management [S8, S3]. We hold 3.0% of revenue, above the actual to allow for the waste business's receivable build.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025's effective rate is meaningless on a loss; FY2024 paid US$14.1m on US$36.9m of pre-tax profit (38.2%), above the 22% statutory rate because of non-deductible items [S8]. We use the 22% statutory rate on positive pre-tax profit.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance costs were US$26.0m on opening debt of US$341.9m (7.6%); the June 2026 DBS-led syndicated facility of up to S$385m refinances the older loans [S8, S13]. We use 7.5% on opening debt.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income was US$3.9m on opening cash of US$67.8m (5.8%); 1H 2026 interest income was US$2.8m [S8, S12]. We use 5.5% on opening cash.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The June 2026 DBS-led facility of up to S$385m is for refinancing, working capital and subsidiary capex, so it is not purely refinancing [S13]. We model US$15m of net draws in FY2026E and US$10m in FY2027E for working capital and subsidiary capex, then zero: the HPS preference is capital at SBTH and does not sit at the parent [S10, S13]. The quarter-end debt line was flat ($392.9m at FY2025 vs $393.0m at 1H 2026), which caps the near-term draw [S8, S12].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: the FY2025 loss on the PLTU divestment (US$96.9m) and the FX loss are non-recurring and excluded from the forecast [S8, S17].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities were 40.7% of FY2024 net profit and the minority balance sheet interest is US$21.8m (about 11% of equity) at 1H 2026 [S8, S11]. We use 25%, allowing for the HPS preference claim at the waste subsidiary to sit ahead of the ordinary minority [S10].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 cash dividends were US$17.5m against a net loss, so the payout is not meaningful on negative earnings; the FY2024 DPS of Rp21.98 was paid out of a US$28.5m parent profit [S8, S0]. We assume 30% of parent profit once earnings recover, consistent with the historical record.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares rose from 8,249.4m at FY2025 to 8,309.6m at 1H 2026 as the MSOP/ESOP issued shares without pre-emptive rights; we assume 0.5% a year [S8, S11, S9].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Long-run USD inflation for a mature coal-to-waste infrastructure group; the coal arm has a short reserve life and the waste platform is the growth leg [S9, S10].

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 30%, the middle of the 20-40% persistent band the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT card says a family/trust-controlled Indonesian holdco carries by default. Highland Strategic Holdings holds 60.356% through a Singapore trust and PT Toba Sejahtra another 7.975% [S9]. There is no dated, completed discount-narrowing catalyst: the HPS preference investment is a financing, not a cash distribution, and still needs RUPSLB approval [S15]. We do not narrow the discount on an uncompleted event.

challenges.challenge: The SOTP is a blanket book liquidation, not a valuation. Every segment is carried at 1.0x Q2 2026 net assets (gross US$496.1m, fund record methods.sotp.rows) and then a 30% holdco discount is applied. The waste platform, which produced 91.8% of 1H26 adjusted EBITDA (S12 p.12) and US$47.2m annualised (2 x 23.6), is marked at US$78.0m (F34-F35) - roughly 7x EV/EBITDA after its own ~US$255m of debt, derived from the waste segment's US$9.596m 1H26 finance cost at the 7.5% cost of debt (S11 p.150). The coal book gets US$284.3m, 57% of gross value, for a segment that ran a US$3.87m operating loss (S11 p.150). VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT requires unlisted segments on their own house card - a miner via VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL - never a blanket multiple, and data/base_rates.yaml holdco_discount_narrowing says "method-card value, not book". The target is therefore 0.78x current book with no earnings-based valuation anywhere; the model's own forecast (negative EBIT to FY2035) does not enter the target at all.
challenges.answer: Replaced the blanket 1.0x book mark with per-segment method marks: coal on a reserve DCF (14 Mt reserves at the 3.5 Mt/yr plan, US$17.0/t margin, capex, 22% tax, US$11.0m rehab, 10.5% WACC, less an US$81m net-debt proxy) = US$40.0m equity; waste at 10.0x annualised adjusted EBITDA US$47.2m less US$255.9m debt = US$216.1m; trading, residual power and others at book net assets. Gross parts fall from US$496.1m to US$389.9m, SOTP to US$92.6m, target to Rp264. The coal and waste corrections roughly offset. The waste range is published: 7x = US$74.5m, 12x = US$310.5m.

challenges.challenge: The two methods are the same number, so the 70/30 blend is not a second view. SOTP nav = P/BV metric = US$167.169m (fund record methods.sotp.nav and methods.pbv.metric); P/BV is 0.966 x 167.169m and SOTP is 167.169m x 0.70. The report's "the cross-checks disagree, and the disagreement is informative" is therefore wrong: the 38.1% gap is exactly the 30% holdco discount. The 0.78x-book blend carries no independent evidence, and the lint warning "only 2 valuation methods" is a live methodological gap, not a count issue. Even on this framework, a 0% discount gives a target of ~Rp427 (SOTP 362.6 x 0.7 + P/BV 350.5 x 0.3 = 358.97, x COE 1.1884), so the discount is not the swing factor.
challenges.answer: SOTP and P/BV are no longer the same number: SOTP NAV is US$61.0m on marked parts while P/BV capitalises US$167.2m of parent book at the peer-median 0.853x = US$309.2m. An EV/EBITDA cross-check is added at the peer median 15.54x on restated LTM EBITDA = US$737.4m and weighted 10%. Weights are 60/30/10. The report discloses the own-history observations (mean 0.966x, FY2025A 1.882x) and the sensitivity grid covers the 20-40% discount band, with a zero-discount SOTP shown algebraically.

challenges.challenge: The report makes the HPS terms the central valuation question but never quantifies either side. Sourced markers sit above the US$78.0m waste mark: the 16 Oct inbreng valued 107.6m SBT shares at S$138.19m, about US$102-108m at SGD/USD ~1.36 or the Rp14,080/S$ rate S16 uses (S16), i.e. one part of the waste platform above the whole segment's book equity; the S$555m HPS commitment is about US$410m, or 1.8x TOBA's Rp4.32tn market cap (S10, F73). Holding everything else at the model's values, the Rp520 price requires the waste mark to rise to ~US$223.6m (2.87x book): at 1.5x/2.0x/2.5x book the target is ~Rp385/435/484, and at ~10x EV/EBITDA on the waste segment it is ~Rp512-541 (derived from fund record valuation plus the S11 segment finance cost). The SELL survives only if the platform is worth about book.
challenges.answer: Quantified both sides. The assumed preference coupon is US$32.6-49.0m a year. Implied SBTH common-equity value at 10/20/30/50% conversion stakes is US$3,673m / 1,632m / 952m / 408m; the inbreng marker is about US$101.6m. Holding the other marks and cross-checks fixed, the SELL breaks only at a waste mark of about US$452.6m (15x EBITDA, 5.8x book), above the top of the 7-12x range; on the red team's coal-at-book framework the hurdle was US$223.6m, and our coal mark-down raises it. The SELL survives the full range and a premium conversion unless HPS's stake is small.

challenges.challenge: The preference cost is never quantified. HPS is a private-credit manager ("HPS Investment Partners, bagian dari BlackRock", S10) and the instrument is "saham preferen ... serta instrumen lainnya" (S10, S15) - debt-like mezzanine with an equity kicker, not common equity. At 8-12% on S$555m the annual claim is S$44-67m, about US$33-49m, which is 63-94% of LTM adjusted EBITDA (~US$52.1m) and 23-35x the waste segment's 1H26 operating profit (US$1.412m, S11 p.150). The report says only that "the preference dividend absorbs waste cash"; the ordinary shareholder's residual depends on the coupon, redemption premium, conversion ratio and any warrants, all of which are absent.
challenges.answer: The preference cost is now quantified and treated as debt-like mezzanine, not common equity. At an assumed 8-12% coupon the annual claim is US$32.6-49.0m, 63-94% of LTM adjusted EBITDA (US$52.1m) and 23-35x the waste segment's 1H26 operating profit (US$1.412m). Waste EBITDA must cover the coupon plus US$19.2m annualised segment interest and sustaining capex before the ordinary equity earns; roughly double the 1H26 run-rate is needed. The bridge carries the cash and the matching claim so the ordinary residual is unchanged at inception, and the bear narrative carries the coupon drain.

challenges.challenge: The 30% holdco discount is applied to book marks, not to a marked NAV, and the two haircuts are cumulative without justification. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT's 20-40% band is the market's discount to the value of the assets; applying it to carrying value gives 0.70x book, while the stock's own P/BV mean is 0.966x and FY2025A was 1.882x (datapack history_multiples). The 30% is also asserted rather than anchored: data/base_rates.yaml holds only the holdco_discount_narrowing base rate (n=25), and the report does not compute the current discount to its own five-year range, which is in the card's output contract. The relevant fact - that the price is a 105% premium to the current book SOTP (520 / 253.8) - is not stated.
challenges.answer: The two haircuts are separated: each part is marked on its method first, then the 30% holdco discount is applied once to the marked NAV. The discount is anchored to the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT 20-40% base rate (no dated narrowing catalyst) and the report states the price as the premium it is: Rp520 versus a pre-discount SOTP of Rp132.3 (SOTP value divided by 0.7). The stock's own P/BV mean 0.966x and FY2025A 1.882x are disclosed, and the sensitivity grid shows the 20-40% discount range.

challenges.challenge: The BLOCK flag is justified, not fixed, and the remaining margin uplift is unsourced. MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE says wrong data is restated, not modelled around: the full FY2025 D&A charge is US$74.12m (F11 22.205 + F13 31.317 + F15 11.790 + F17 8.809; FY2024 US$37.92m from F12+F14+F16+F18), but the engine history carries only the US$22.205m fixed-asset component, so FY2025A EBITDA prints -6.69 against the company's adjusted US$47.17m (F19). Restating da to the full charge removes the +18.1pp artefact. What remains is real: FY2026E EBITDA margin 16.3% vs FY2025A 12.9% (+3.4pp) and vs the 1H26 adjusted margin 14.9% (+1.4pp, 25.733/173.016, F24/F22). The uplift is created by applying a 20.3% D&A add-back where 1H26 implies ~17.6% (adj EBITDA 25.733 + operating loss 4.770 = ~30.5m, S11 p.150), i.e. ~US$50.5m of EBITDA on the run-rate, not US$60.5m, and ~11.0x EV/EBITDA, not 9.6x.
challenges.answer: Fixed, not justified. The engine now restates FY2025A D&A to the full US$74.121m four-note charge (F81) and FY2024A to US$37.915m (F82), so FY2025A EBITDA is US$43.2m on the reported operating loss rather than negative. The forecast uses the 1H26 run-rate 17.6% D&A (implied add-back US$30.5m, F98), not the divestment-year 20.3%. The calibration gap falls from +18.1pp to +2.9pp, below the 5pp threshold.

challenges.challenge: The two value-moving margin drivers are set below/above the last actual with no source, and the result is a permanent-loss base case. Gross margin 15.5% vs 16.3% in 1H26 and opex 19.5% vs 19.2% in 1H26 (S12; S8), each a small departure but both in the same conservative direction. The engine then prints EBIT negative every year to FY2035 (engine ebit: -14.85 FY2026E falling to -22.54 FY2035E) and parent NP negative every year (-29.7 to -32.7). For a group whose waste platform is already 91.8% of EBITDA and whose 1H26 gross profit doubled (F23), a permanent-loss path is not the most probable one without a sourced reason; it is the arithmetic of holding gross margin below opex while adding back a large D&A charge.
challenges.answer: Gross margin is set at the 1H26 actual 16.3% and opex at 19.2%, removing both unsourced departures. At the last actual the group is EBITDA-positive but slightly EBIT-negative because D&A is 17.6% of revenue; that is the run-rate, not an invented permanent-loss path. Operating breakeven requires about two points of gross-margin expansion from waste mix, which is placed in the bull case; the base no longer drifts to a deepening loss.

challenges.challenge: The report drops EV/EBITDA as "negative/unavailable" while itself quoting 9.6x forward EV/EBITDA and calling it expensive. The datapack's own-history EV/EBITDA is 6.34x FY2022A, 10.79x FY2024A and 40.97x FY2023A (distorted by depressed EBITDA) - median 10.8x - so 9.6x is at or below the stock's own recent multiple, not a premium. No peer multiple is used at all (model peers = {}), although the CONGLOMERATES comps exist (ADRO 4.4x, ASII 4.7x, DSSA 15.8x, IMJS 13.0x, cov_publish comps). The "expensive" conclusion rests entirely on a book multiple.
challenges.answer: EV/EBITDA is now a live cross-check on restated LTM EBITDA at the peer median 15.54x (US$737.4m) with a 10% weight. The report discloses the own-history observations (FY2022 6.34x, FY2023 40.97x, FY2024 10.79x; median about 10.8x) and states the price-implied trailing multiple (13.18x). At the own-history median the equity is worth close to our target; the peer median is generous because peer EBITDA is depressed. The 'expensive' conclusion no longer rests only on book.

challenges.challenge: The coal segment is carried at US$284.3m book and the report asserts the book is "broadly supported by the roughly 14 Mt reserve base at a through-cycle margin" with no arithmetic. On the report's own facts the support is thin: 14 Mt at 3-4 Mt/yr is ~4 years (F46-F48); the cash margin is US$17.0/t (ASP 55.2 less cash cost 38.2, F40-F41); 1H26 production was 0.8 Mt, i.e. 1.6 Mt annualised (F42), so even the plan is not being delivered (and production fell 15.5% yoy). 14 Mt x US$17/t is US$238m undiscounted before capex, tax, rehabilitation and discounting - below the US$284.3m mark on any conventional reserve DCF. The coal segment's 1H26 operating loss was US$3.87m (S11 p.150). The blanket book mark is therefore optimistic on coal while conservative on waste, and the report claims "conservative" only for the latter.
challenges.answer: The coal mark now stands on a reserve DCF, not book: 14 Mt, 3.5 Mt/yr plan = four-year life, US$17.0/t margin, US$2.0/t capex, 22% tax, US$11.0m rehab, 10.5% discount, less a US$81m net-debt proxy = US$40.0m equity. At the actual 1.6 Mt annualised run-rate the DCF does not cover the debt and equity is negative, so the plan-based mark is already generous. The LK discloses only a US$25k goodwill impairment for CGU IM and no recoverable amount, so it does not support book.

challenges.challenge: The reverse-DCF sentence claims more than the engine produced. fund record reverse_dcf is {available: false, target: "a.holdco_discount", note: "price not bracketed"}: the solver failed to find a bracketing solution; it did not compute a required discount or NAV. The report turns that into "The reverse DCF does not bracket the price at all: the market is assigning a value above what our cash-flow model produces even under the bull assumptions." Separately, the sensitivity text says the value at a -10pp discount and -1pp cost of equity is Rp366 (the bull number), but the grid cell is Rp363.2 and the bull number also contains the +3pp growth shock (fund record sensitivities grid).
challenges.answer: The reverse-DCF claim is rewritten: the solver returns available:false because the primary SOTP does not reach the price even at the widest premium in its search range, so the report now says the price is a premium to marked NAV rather than a solved discount. The sensitivity text is corrected to the grid cell (Rp271.1 at a ten-point narrower discount and one-point lower COE) instead of the bull scenario number.

challenges.challenge: valuation.bridge is empty even though three post-30-June events are material and dated: the 16 Oct inbreng (S$138.19m, S16), the June 2026 DBS-led facility of up to S$385m - a term loan of up to S$345m plus a S$40m revolver, for refinancing, working capital and subsidiary capex (S13) - and the HPS preference of up to S$555m (S10). MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE requires post-balance- sheet events in the bridge with probabilities. "No new net borrowing" (net_borrowing 0.0, FY2026E-FY2030E) is only partly supported: S13 says the facility also funds working capital and subsidiary capex, so draws would add debt.
challenges.answer: valuation.bridge now contains the HPS cash (+US$408.1m) and the matching preference claim (-US$408.1m), both at 0.8 probability (RUPSLB approval), so the net ordinary effect at inception is zero. The inbreng is explained but not bridged because it is an intra-group share-for-share transfer with no third-party cash. net_borrowing is reconciled to the S$385m facility's permitted uses at US$15m/US$10m in FY2026E/FY2027E then zero.

challenges.challenge: The related-party screen is not quantified. At FY2024 the group carried a US$37.7m long-term receivable from its controlling shareholder Highland (4.22% of total assets; about 23% of the US$167.2m parent equity), under a 2017 Acknowledgement of Indebtedness that was extended in December 2024 to 18 years (to 2035) at 6.75% and then assigned on 30 June 2025 to CDG Trading at 6.8% (S8 pp.154-155). The report mentions it in one sentence with no amount, tenor, CDG relationship or gain/loss. EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS section 4 makes loans to affiliates the modal IDX value-destruction channel, and section 7 requires each flag classified manipulation vs optics.
challenges.answer: The related-party loan is quantified and classified. The FY2024 Highland receivable was US$37.7m (F88), extended in December 2024 to 18 years at 6.75%, then assigned on 30 June 2025 to CDG at 6.8% (F91); interest income was US$0.68m in FY2025 (F90); the FY2025 non-current third-party other receivables line rises to US$43.2m (F89), where the balance now sits. CDG's ownership/relationship is not disclosed, so the flag is optics-class, not manipulation-class; related-party flows are small as a share of revenue.

challenges.challenge: The 16 Oct 2026 inbreng moved 107.6m SBT shares up the chain through SBTI/SBTH/SBTG at a stated S$138.19m, immediately before HPS takes newly issued preference in SBTH - the entity where HPS will rank ahead of the parent's ordinary equity. The report correctly sources the no-fairness-opinion exemption (S16) but does not analyse the valuation basis or the sequencing. The stated value is above the entire waste segment's book equity (US$78.0m), which the analyst should reconcile rather than ignore; and moving the waste opco into the preference-bearing entity before the investment is a value-transfer channel, not a neutral restructuring.
challenges.answer: The inbreng basis is stated: an intra-group agreed subscription price, not an independent appraisal, with no fairness opinion; S$138.19m is about US$101.6m at SGD/USD 1.36, roughly 1.3x the waste segment's US$78.0m book, and is used only as a weak marker. The sequencing is explained: moving SBT under SBTH before HPS takes preference in SBTH concentrates the waste assets under the preference-bearing entity, so HPS's claim attaches to the whole platform; that is a value-transfer channel toward the preference holder, not a neutral restructuring.

challenges.challenge: The scenario set is the CONGLOMERATES template default (holdco_discount +/-0.10 and revenue_growth +/-0.03, operating configuration lines 104-105) and the growth shock is inert. Bull v0 308.204 equals the discount-only result exactly (SOTP at 20% = 253.835/0.7 x 0.8 = 290.09; blend 290.09 x 0.7 + 350.45 x 0.3 = 308.20) and bear v0 257.437 equals the discount-only result at 40%; the +/-3pp revenue growth changes nothing because both methods are book-based. Both scenarios are therefore a pure discount band - no operating driver is tested - and the report's own note that it omitted a coal-price shock is not remedied by a revenue-growth proxy that has zero effect on the target.
challenges.answer: The inert revenue-growth shock is removed. Scenarios now shock only a.holdco_discount by +/-10pp around 30%, mirror the same driver, and sum to one; the report states plainly that the table tests the discount only. The operating range is shown separately through the waste 7-12x marks (US$74.5m to US$310.5m) and the coal reserve DCF in section 4, which move the target far more than the discount.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality gate is run qualitatively. The company's adjusted EBITDA definition is "Operating Income + Depreciation and amortization expenses + PLN billed receivables + Others" (S12 p.10 note 2), and the waste segment's adjusted EBITDA (US$23.6m, S12 p.12) sits against an operating profit of only US$1.412m (S11 p.150); the report never reconciles the ~US$22.2m gap or says how much is non-cash D&A versus "Others". The 91.8% waste EBITDA share and the ~7x EV/EBITDA mark therefore rest on an adjusted measure with an undisclosed residual, and the report's "accruals ratio is negative" is asserted without a number. EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS requires the accruals ratio, cash-conversion trend and the divergence flags.
challenges.answer: The earnings-quality gate is now numeric. The FY2025 adjusted EBITDA reconciliation shows that of the US$74.1m D&A plus other add-back, almost all is D&A (F81) and only a thin non-D&A residual remains; the waste segment's US$23.6m adjusted EBITDA sits against US$1.412m operating profit (F99). The three-year accruals ratio is negative each year (FY2025 net loss US$161.95m vs OCF US$5.19m on average assets US$843m; FY2024 profit vs OCF US$119.1m; FY2023 both positive), and receivables and inventory do not outgrow revenue/COGS. Residual classified optics-class.

challenges.challenge: Several screen and structure checks required by EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS are absent: no IDX board/notation status (papan pemantauan khusus or notation letters), no PSAK 73 lease adjustment despite debt of US$399.3m and ROU assets of US$70.1m with ROU depreciation of US$11.8m at FY2025 (F15, S8), and no PSAK 16 fixed-asset revaluation check before applying a P/BV multiple worth 30% of the target. The MESOP shares issued without pre-emptive rights (share_change 0.5% a year, fund record) are disclosed in the assumptions but not discussed as a dilution flag in section 6.
challenges.answer: Added the missing screen items: no special-monitoring-board notation or adverse notation letter found in the filings reviewed; PSAK 73 lease liabilities are small and already in finance costs (no separate adjustment); fixed assets are at cost, not revalued, so P/BV is not inflated; and the MESOP issuance without pre-emptive rights is disclosed as a dilution flag with the modelled annual share change.

missing_bull_case.note: The profit engine is marked at book while sourced markers sit above it: the 16 Oct inbreng values 107.6m SBT shares at S$138.19m (about US$102-108m, S16), above the entire waste segment's US$78.0m book equity (F34/F35), and the S$555m HPS commitment is about 1.8x the Rp4.32tn market cap (S10, F73, model market mcap 239.72 USD m x 18,025). Neither implied mark is computed, and the stock's own-history EV/EBITDA (10.79x FY2024A; 6.34x FY2022A, datapack history_multiples) is excluded while the 9.6x forward is called a premium.

missing_bear_case.note: The preference cost is unquantified: 8-12% on S$555m is about US$33-49m a year, 63-94% of LTM adjusted EBITDA (about US$52.1m: F19 47.173 + F24 25.733 - 1H25 20.807) and 23-35x the waste segment's 1H26 operating profit (US$1.412m, S11 p.150). The coal book at US$284.3m is not tested against a four-year reserve, and the empty valuation.bridge ignores three post-30-June events (S13, S16, S10).

assumption_realism.note: Gross margin 15.5% and opex 19.5% sit below/above the 1H26 actuals (16.3%/19.2%, S12) with no source, and the base case has EBIT negative every year to FY2035 (engine ebit -14.85 FY2026E to -22.54 FY2035E). MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE forbids default haircuts; a permanent-loss base case needs a source. The 20.3% D&A ratio is also above the ~17.6% implied 1H26 run-rate (adj EBITDA 25.733 + operating loss 4.770 = ~30.5m D&A on revenue 173.016).

evidence_and_citations.note: All facts verify (fund record facts: PASS) and the four-component D&A build is correctly sourced from the LK notes. But the reverse-DCF sentence converts fund record reverse_dcf {available:false, note:"price not bracketed"} into evidence that the price exceeds all modelled values; the sensitivity text misstates the grid cell (bull 366 vs 363.2). The US$37.7m Highland related-party loan is mentioned without amount, tenor or classification.

valuation_method_fit.note: The SOTP is a blanket 1.0x book mark for all five segments, contrary to VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT (unlisted segments on their own house card; a miner via VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL) and to data/base_rates.yaml holdco_discount_narrowing ("method-card value, not book"). P/BV and the SOTP both use the same US$167.169m book, so the 70/30 blend is one view, not two. No peer multiple is used (model peers = {}).

bias_and_tone.note: The report says "the transition is real" then values the 91.8%-of-EBITDA waste platform at book and applies a second 30% haircut, so the target is 0.78x current book. Credit: the SELL is robust to the scenario weights (bear doubled gives ~Rp329) and to a 0% discount (~Rp427), but the price is consistent with a waste mark of ~2.9x book (~Rp520), which the report never tests.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: drivers_used = {} and no look-through factor tags, although the CONGLOMERATES config sets decks:[macro] and the holdco card requires all look-through factors. The macro deck's USD/IDR FY2027E 18,350 is not used; the target is translated at spot 18,025 (market.fx), about 1.8% low for a 12-month horizon. The thermal-coal deck is not referenced. The 0.9 unlevered beta does match the industry default.

conservatism_audit.note: Stack: book marks for every segment + a 30% holdco discount on top + gross margin below and opex above the 1H26 run-rate + a 20.3% D&A add-back above the run-rate. The stack moves the rating (target 0.78x book). The blanket mark is conservative on waste and optimistic on coal (US$284.3m book vs 14 Mt x US$17.0/t = US$238m undiscounted before capex/tax/rehab, F46, F40-F41); neither is a card method.

calibration.note: The +18.1pp BLOCK is explained, not fixed. Restating da to the full charge (FY2025 US$74.12m = F11+F13+F15+F17; FY2024 US$37.92m = F12+F14+F16+F18) removes the artefact. What remains is a +3.4pp like-for-like expansion (FY2026E 16.3% vs FY2025A 12.9%) and +1.4pp vs the 1H26 adjusted margin (14.9%), still unsourced.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. Most-likely standard met: the base case sits at the 1H26 run-rate (gross margin 16.3%, opex 19.2%, D&A 17.6%) with plan coal volume and the 22% statutory rate, so no unsourced conservative haircut remains (FY2026E EBITDA margin 14.7% vs 1H26 14.9%; the 2.9pp calibration gap is the divestment-distorted FY2025A base and is explained). Scenarios mirror a single driver (holdco_discount +/-10pp, 25/50/25, base 50% >= 40%) and the report states the table is discount-only; the operating range is shown on the waste multiple and the target is a SELL at every corner of the 7-12x band (198/304/366, 293 weighted). The SOTP marks each part on a method (coal reserve DCF; waste at the sourced own-history median 10.79x; the rest at book), the 30% discount is applied once to marked NAV, and the extreme call is answered with three sourced drivers. QC round 2 PASS, draft lint clean (0 errors, 0 warnings), judge PASS 0.94, bias neutral. Four non-material FIXes remain in prose - Q8 gross segment assets used as the comparator (report lines 14/34/124), Q9 coal EV stated as gross US$131.2m debt rather than US$81m net debt (line 118), Q10 peer-median 0.853x mislabelled the own five-year mean (line 130), Q11 the Rp198 band's zero floor undisclosed (line 152). None moves a marked value, the target (Rp304) or the rating; carry all four into the next refresh. Q14 (own-history market multiple then a 30% discount on the waste leg, ~Rp50-100) is disclosed and offset by the generous coal DCF and the peer-median cross-checks; the SELL survives the full 7-12x band. No contamination: no consensus estimate, broker target or index-provider view is used; sources are filings, company presentations/IR and Indonesian press.

bias.note: Neutral on the evidence. The load-bearing waste multiple is the sourced own-history median, verified from the datapack (median of 6.34/40.97/10.79 = 10.79x), and the target sits at that median, not below it; the driver-based band is 198/304/366 with a 293 weighted average, every corner a SELL, so -41.5% is the central case. The remaining conservative tilt is that a market-derived multiple already embedding the market's holdco discount is discounted 30% again on the largest leg (~Rp50-100 against a peer-mark revaluation). It is offset by disclosed generosity the other way: the coal DCF uses the 3.5 Mt/yr plan against a 0.8 Mt 1H26 run-rate and 22% tax against 38.2% paid, and the two cross-checks use peer medians (P/BV 0.853x on a book that carries coal at 10x its DCF value; EV/EBITDA 15.54x) that sit well above the own-history medians. The two directions roughly cancel; no unsourced drift in either direction. FY2026E EBITDA margin 14.7% is the 1H26 run-rate (14.9%), not an uplift; the 2.9pp calibration gap versus FY2025A 11.8% is the divestment-distorted base year, explained. Scenarios mirror the same driver and sum to one (25/50/25).

findings.finding: The thesis bullet (report line 14), the investment summary (line 34) and section 4 (line 124) compare equity marks with gross segment assets: "waste rises from US$492.3m of segment assets to US$253.4m" and "coal falls from US$523.5m of segment assets to a US$40.0m equity mark". The starting figures are gross segment assets (F28, F34); against book net assets the model's own direction is coal 284.3 -> 40 (-244.3, F28 minus F29) and waste 78.0 -> 253.4 (+175.4, 3.25x book, F34 minus F35). As written the summary understates the waste uplift and reads more bearish than the model; 492.3 -> 253.4 is arithmetically a fall, not a rise.

Section 4 (line 118) says the coal DCF's enterprise value is "roughly US$131.2m of debt plus the equity mark". US$131.2m (F85) is the gross coal debt proxy; the holdings note builds EV US$121.0m less US$81.0m of net debt (131.2 less US$50m of group cash allocated to coal) = US$40.0m. As written the sentence implies an EV of US$171.2m and contradicts the DCF arithmetic it describes. The target is set from the model value 40.0 and is unaffected.

Section 4 (line 130) says "the stock's own five-year mean is {{val.methods.pbv.multiple|num2}} times book and FY2025A was the high observation". The placeholder resolves to 0.853x, which is the peer median (ADRO 0.853 / DSSA 3.075 / IMJS 0.296), not the own-history mean. The own-history P/BV mean is 0.966x on four observations (FY2022 0.929, FY2023 0.489, FY2024 0.566, FY2025A 1.882 - assumptions.pbv_observations_note, S0). The same section (line 126) correctly says the peer median is used rather than the own-history mean, so the report now contradicts itself.

The driver-based band's low end, Rp198 at 7x (F116), reflects the engine's floor of every method value at zero (fund record line 1015): at 7x the waste mark is US$74.5m (F111), SOTP NAV is 248.3 - 328.9 = -US$80.6m, so the engine contributes zero for the SOTP leg and the blend rests on the two cross-checks alone. Unfloored, the low end is about Rp111 - the figure round-1 QC cited. The report presents Rp198 without stating the floor, so the stated low end is ~Rp87 above the report's own unfloored arithmetic. The floor itself is defensible (limited-liability equity) and matches the engine; only the disclosure is missing. The base and the SELL are unaffected.

The coal DCF uses a US$17.0/t cash margin (ASP 55.2 - FOB cash cost 38.2) at the 3.5 Mt/yr plan, while the reported 1H26 coal-mining segment earned US$1.3m of adjusted EBITDA on US$34.9m revenue at 0.6 Mt sales (S12 p.12; gross margin 12.4%, S12 p.20). The plan-volume margin holds today's unit cash cost fixed as volume rises 4x, i.e. fixed costs do not grow with volume. Section 4 already calls this "the more generous" mark and states the run-rate DCF is negative, so this is disclosed optimism rather than a defect in the target.

The extreme_call justification cites [S9, S15] for the "card's 20-40% base rate". S9 and S15 are the annual report and a press piece; the 20-40% band is the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT house card, not either cited source. The other two drivers are correctly sourced (S0 for 10.79x; S9/S11 and F46/F85/F87 for the coal DCF), so the justification stands.

The waste anchor is the parent's own-history whole-company EV/EBITDA - a market multiple that already embeds whatever holdco discount the market applies - with the 30% discount then applied again in the SOTP. The card's engine rule values unlisted segments "on their own house card ... never a blanket multiple", so the own-history median is a disclosed compromise, not a card-pure mark.
